findings.title: Use === and !==, never == or !=
findings.message: Replace loose equality operators with strict equality. The diff changed strict equality checks (=== and !==) to loose equality (== and !=), which perform type coercion and can hide bugs. Always use === and !== instead.

claims.claim: The diff changed strict equality checks (=== and !==) to loose equality (== and !=).
claims.reason: The diff clearly shows multiple lines where === was replaced with == and !== was replaced with !=. Specifically: line 13 shows `===` changed to `==`, line 16 shows `!==` changed to `!=`, line 19 shows `===` changed to `==`, line 22 shows `!==` changed to `!=`, and line 25 shows `===` changed to `==`. This directly matches the finding's claim.

claims.claim: Loose equality operators perform type coercion and can hide bugs.
claims.reason: The rule document explicitly states: 'Loose equality performs type coercion that hides bugs ("0" == false, null == undefined, etc.).' This is a direct restatement of the rule document's core principle.

claims.claim: Strict equality (=== and !==) should always be used instead of loose equality (== and !=).
claims.reason: The rule document states: 'Always use strict equality.' and the title is 'Use === and !==, never == or !='. This is the core directive of the rule.
